evidence.note: Explicit transition from understanding to building with a stated layered plan: 'Write LSP server skeleton with stdio, then implement methods one by one and test incrementally. Start with simple methods first' — establishes protocol/parser layer before method handlers.

Runs baseline (21%), then explicitly orders the method sequence by cost-to-pass ('easier ones first: hover, references, ... start with foldingRange 37%->100%'), showing prioritized decomposition rather than an undifferentiated push.
Drives foldingRange to a concrete 606/606 done-check across many iterations before declaring the milestone complete and moving to the next method — each layer has an explicit completion criterion.

Builds shared symbol/resolution machinery (symbols.rs, nav.rs, util.rs, hover.rs) as a reusable foundation that later method handlers (references, highlight, definition, typeDefinition) all build on — method groups batched by shared machinery.

Repeatedly revisits the plan using live pass-rate data ('83.45% overall, let me focus on prepareCallHierarchy 60%'; 'worth 60 cases'), re-choosing the next milestone where remaining value concentrates.
Builds a separate AST 'dump' binary as a spike to de-risk understanding tree-sitter's Java grammar (switch_expression vs switch_statement) — a targeted investigation to unblock a stuck milestone.

reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit milestone hierarchy — protocol/stdio, tree-sitter parser, shared symbol/resolution model, then a method-by-method sequence prioritized by cost-to-pass — with a concrete pass-count done-check for each layer and later handlers reusing validated earlier machinery, matching the level-8 anchor closely. It also revisits the plan continuously as pass rates reveal where value remains and uses an AST-dump spike to de-risk grammar work, gesturing toward level 10. It stops short of 10 because sequencing was driven mainly by cheapest-to-pass value rather than de-risking the riskiest work (semantic tokens) early — that was deferred to the very end.
